speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and did it begin after any specific injury or trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, that sounds like a classic "jammed finger" mechanism. To help me rule out a fracture or a dislocation, can you tell me if you are able to fully straighten and bend the finger, or does it feel stuck?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the inability to flex the DIP joint after a hyperextension injury strongly suggests a mallet finger. I will now order an X-ray to confirm if there is an associated fracture at the base of the distal phalanx.

REQUEST TEST: Right Hand X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms no fracture, so this is a pure tendon injury known as mallet finger. To be thorough, can you tell me if there is any numbness or tingling in the fingertip, or any open wounds over the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since there are no fractures, nerve issues, or open wounds, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
